subject: Error in generating Wallace code files

messages.author: c02c2d9fc9455f9a
messages.subject: Error in generating Wallace code files
parts:
Hello!

First of all, I wanted to say that I'm excited to use this program to help develop lab activities for the course I am teaching this fall. I am working on developing example files and learning how to use the program and am running into an error in downloading the output code from the model.

The error I am getting is 
"Warning in options$echo && options$ eval :
'length(x) = 3 > 1' in coercion to 'logical(1)'
Quitting from lines 399-401 (userReport2.Rmd)

Warning: Error in if: the condition has length > 1
[No stack trace available]

I am attaching the following files:
  • Output from the R Console, including the results from the object "version"
  • The input .csv file I am using for running wallace
The steps I am taking in the program are as follows:
  • Step 1: Module User-specified: input - attached .csv
  • Step 2: Remove occurrences by ID: Remove OccID 489
  • Step 3: WorldClim BioClims: 30 arcsec
  • Step 4a: Select Study Region: 0.5 degree bounding box
  • Step 4b: 10000 samples
  • Step 5: Non-spatial partitions: 4 k-folds
  • Step 6: BioClim
  • Step 7: Map prediction: No threshold (but .Rmd error message is unchanged regardless of which method I choose)
  • Session Code: Download Session Code (does not matter which output I select).
Thanks for any assistance you can offer. I updated all packages today and still run into the same error message.

Sincerely,
Dakota

messages.author: 881c0dd9c7b0d196
messages.subject: Re: Error in generating Wallace code files
parts:
Hi Dakota,
I followed your workflow and was not able to reproduce the error (I've attached a sample RMD I was able to generate). I will flag Gonzalo to take a look at the error when he is back from vacation.
In the meantime try updating the 'knitr' package. Also, if you are interested, you can also try updating to Wallace v2 and see if that version also gives you issues downloading the session code. It's a developmental version, but you should be able to run your workflow without issues. You can find instructions on how to install here. The only difference is you will need to edit the csv of your occurrence data; the column header 'name' will need to be changed to 'scientific_name' to work properly. 

-Bethany
PS: Just to put a face to the Wallace account, we met at the sky island panel discussion at ASM
